paragraphs: Elmi Muller is a South African transplant surgeon and Dean of the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences at Stellenbosch University. In 2008, she pioneered the world's first programme to transplant kidneys from HIV-positive donors into HIV-positive recipients at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town — a decision that broke with medical convention and went on to save thousands of lives, reshaping global transplant guidelines in the process.

She is past president of the Southern African Transplantation Society and serves as vice-president of The Transplantation Society (TTS). Her work has been recognised internationally, including a feature in The Lancet and the Shoprite Checkers Woman of the Year award.
